chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Mūsā ibn Ṭalḥah, from Abī Bakr ibn ʿĪsā ibn Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, who said:

I was in the mosque when a جنازة (funeral bier) was brought, and I wanted to perform prayer over it. Then Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام came, placed his elbow on my chest, and kept pushing me until he brought me out of the mosque. Then he said: “O Abā Bakr, funeral prayers are not performed over the dead in the mosque.”
So the correct understanding of this report is that it indicates a degree of reprehensibility, not prohibition.

key_terms.أُصَلِّيَ: to perform salat (prayer), here referring to prayer over the deceased
key_terms.الْجَنَائِزَ: funeral prayers or the deceased over whom prayer is performed
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikedness; an act considered reprehensible but not forbidden
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque; the place in which the funeral prayer is being discussed
key_terms.بِجِنَازَةٍ: a funeral bier or deceased brought for funeral prayer

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform funeral prayer over a جنازة inside the mosque in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report concerns the ruling of performing prayer over a جنازة inside the mosque. It indicates, according to the compiler’s closing statement, that such an act is disliked rather than strictly forbidden, showing a juristic distinction between karāhah and ḥaẓr.
